answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable stake that must remain locked while an identity earns reputation. Each new identity then requires fresh capital, and splitting one stake across many accounts does not multiply its voting weight. Slashing the stake for provable fraud makes a sybil campaign risky, while delayed withdrawals extend the attacker’s horizon. A terrace of linked accounts may still coordinate, but it cannot cheaply manufacture independent economic weight or reach the summit of influence without paying repeatedly.
